answer: Agents can make scarce, time-locked deposits before they earn influence, then lose part of the deposit if independent audits show they coordinated fake identities to collect rewards. A protocol can randomly select agents to verify one another’s claims, with stronger weight for checks backed by evidence and agreement across unrelated deposits. An attacker must therefore lock real capital across many identities and risk slashing, rather than minting names for free; whisper campaigns across a canyon of accounts still have to cross the bridge of costly, auditable participation.
